title: Interpretable weight-space programming builds transparent transformers and brain encoding models
read_level: full main text (Secs 1-6) plus appendix Tables A2 and A7; other appendix model descriptions skimmed
why_wsp: A Claude Code (or Gemini) agent writes every weight of small transformers, and hand-crafted feature networks for brain encoding, directly in code with training forbidden, iterating on a fixed evaluator's score (iWSP).
domain: algorithmic tasks and NLP classification; brain encoding models (visual fMRI, language fMRI, auditory ECoG)
editor: Claude Code with Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 (algorithmic/NLP); Gemini 4 Carbon (visual cortex); Claude Opus 4.7 (language fMRI, ECoG); Opus 5.5 as auditor and rebuilder
target: GPT-style transformer, 'three layers of width 64 by default' (architecture editable), final algorithmic models median 166 parameters; NLP models ~190,000 parameters; visual model <100,000 explicit parameters, 9,996 features; ECoG model 3,852 features
interface: code/tensor tools (write_weights(model, task) in Python; closed-form parameter setting)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (visible-set metric each iteration, 30-50 iterations per algorithmic/NLP run; 600 visual; 902 ECoG)
self_editing: no; agent writes external small networks
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: All weights written from scratch: "Writes every weight" (Fig 1a); "The model parameters must be set in closed form." (Sec 2)

headline_results.quote: All 26 runs on algorithmic tasks reach 100% accuracy both on the visible set and the hidden set
the smallest model that reaches 100% visible accuracy has a median of 166 parameters (Fig. 2c), and in the median run it is 29 times smaller than the first model to reach 100%
a median of 166 parameters for Opus, 41,600 for Sonnet and 100,000 for Haiku

headline_results.claim: NLP: 3 of 4 tasks above majority; paraphrase fails
headline_results.quote: on 3 of the 4 NLP datasets iWSP builds models that achieve respectable performance well above a naive majority baseline (it fails on the relatively difficult Paraphrase task)
headline_results.where: Sec 3; Fig 2a (figure values TREC 87, Sentiment 72, Paraphrase 66, Inference 58; figure only)

headline_results.quote: all 13 rebuilt models (with 2 seeds each) reach 100% hidden accuracy on the algorithmic tasks, and on NLP tasks rebuilt models lose about 1.4 points of hidden accuracy on average

headline_results.claim: Visual cortex: beats interpretable baselines on unseen NSD
headline_results.quote: iWSP beats all 7 interpretable baselines in both early (0.443 versus 0.400 for the best baseline) and ventral visual cortex (0.317 versus 0.256)
iWSP matches black-box accuracy in early visual cortex while trailing in ventral visual cortex (0.391)

headline_results.claim: Language fMRI confound found via position features
headline_results.quote: performance suddenly jumps from 0.067 to 0.104 in a single step ... these position features alone reach about 0.090, above even the strong GPT-2 XL black-box baseline

headline_results.claim: ECoG: below Whisper alone, adds unique variance
headline_results.quote: iWSP starts at 0.039 with a plain gammatone cochleagram and ends at 0.074, below the 0.082 of Whisper
raising performance from 0.070 to 0.075 (this gain of 0.0052 has a 95% interval of 0.0039 to 0.0064 from a bootstrap over electrodes)

cost.claim: Total about $17,500 at API list prices
cost.quote: In total, the paper's experiments cost about $17,500 at API list prices, including estimated exploratory runs

baselines_and_controls: Majority-class baseline (NLP); three Claude model sizes; rebuild-without-description control; seven classical interpretable visual baselines, combined ridge, AlexNet; GPT-2 XL (language fMRI); Whisper-large-v3 and one-shot 'textbook' acoustic features written by Opus 5.5 without feedback (ECoG).
runs_and_variance: Algorithmic/NLP: "We run iWSP on each task twice with each of Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5"; rebuilds 2 per task; neuroscience: error bars as SEM over subjects, bootstrap over electrodes for ECoG gain; single search per neuro setting.
robustness_of_edits: Generalization tested: hidden sets, zero-shot transfer to NSD and held-out subjects; ECoG hidden set and five more patients. Not tested for fine-tuning or quantization. Paper notes "100% performance on our eval tasks does not guarantee correct outputs on all inputs" (Sec 3).
verification: LLM-judge audit of every saved model for training/rule violations; rerunning weight-writing code on altered task data to check weights are independent of data (Table A2: Sonnet had 50 iterations whose weights depend on labels, excluded); 200-word description rebuild test. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: "For algorithmic problems, the agent tends to implement known algorithms rather than conceiving of new ideas" (Sec 3); Limitations: "current agents do not invent genuinely new computational principles".
limitations_stated: Agents recombine known motifs rather than invent new principles; shallow motifs rather than deep hierarchies; relies on faithfulness of agent's written explanations; slow and costly search; observational neuroscience with few subjects and no causal interventions; harness cannot block training, rules are audited afterward.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. Sparks of Weight-Space Programming [51]
notes_for_survey: Extends WSP to a closed-loop, interpretability-constrained setting where the agent writes all weights in code against a fixed evaluator, with an audit (data-independence rerun) and a 200-word rebuild test as interpretability checks. Applied beyond toy tasks to brain encoding, where it surfaced a scan-position confound in a language fMRI dataset.
